title: How a Fire Extinguisher Works in 60 Seconds 🧯🔥 #shorts
description:
A home fire extinguisher is a can of dry powder pushed by squeezed nitrogen gas. Pull the pin, squeeze the lever, and the gas drives the powder up a siphon tube and onto the flames, where it smothers the fuel and stops the burning reaction. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#fireextinguisher #firesafety #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A home fire extinguisher can empty in about *ten seconds*.

steps.label: Inside
steps.text: Inside, *dry powder* sits under *nitrogen* gas, squeezed to over ten times normal air pressure.

steps.label: Trigger
steps.text: Pull the *pin* and squeeze the *lever*, and it pushes a valve open.

steps.label: Spray
steps.text: The gas forces powder up a *siphon tube* and out of the *nozzle*.

steps.label: Triangle
steps.text: Fire needs *heat*, *fuel* and oxygen. Break one side, and it dies.

steps.label: Smother
steps.text: The powder coats the fuel, *cuts off oxygen*, and *interrupts* the burning reaction.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Pressure, powder, *smother*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
